ety.text: From Italian arsenale, from Arabic دَار الصِّنَاعَة (dār aṣ-ṣināʕa, “manufacturing shop”), from دَار (dār) + صِنَاعَة (ṣināʕa).

senses.d: A military establishment for the storing, development, manufacturing, testing, or repairing of arms, ammunition, and other war materiel; an armoury.
A stock of weapons, especially all the weapons that a nation possesses.
A store or supply of anything.
Any supply of aid collected to prepare a person or army for hardship.
ex: He arrived with a large arsenal of cleansers and tools, and got right to work.

ety.text: From Arabic دَار الصِّنَاعَة (dār aṣ-ṣināʕa, “industry house, manufacturing shop”), from دَار (dār) + صِنَاعَة (ṣināʕa). The form could be due to formal assimilation to words with -ale, with reanalysis of the initial d as d' (“of”). Compare darsena.
From Arabic دَار الصِّنَاعَة (dār aṣ-ṣināʕa, “industry house, manufacturing shop”) (via Andalusian Arabic), from دَار (dār) + صِنَاعَة (ṣināʕa). Compare dársena and atarazana.

Arabic خَزَنَ (ḵazana)der. Arabic مَخْزَن (maḵzan) Arabic مَخَازِن (maḵāzin)bor. Italian magazzino From Arabic مَخَازِن pl (maḵāzin), plural of مَخْزَن (maḵzan, “storeroom, storehouse”), noun of place from خَزَنَ (ḵazana, “to store, to stock, to lay up”). Compare Sicilian magasenu.
